conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Maya, and I’m the perinatal mental-health clinician here. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s a brief, 10-question check-in that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling in the past week since your baby arrived. Everything you share stays between us unless there’s an immediate safety concern, so please answer as openly as feels safe for you. We’ll keep the conversation conversational, and if any question feels hard we can pause or rephrase. Ready to start?

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly… not very often. I used to laugh a lot—my husband and I would joke around all the time—but lately it feels like I’m just going through the motions. Maybe once or twice this week I sort of chuckled, but even then it felt forced, like I was pretending to enjoy it. Most of the time I’m too tired or just… heavy, I guess.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I mean, I laughed a little when the baby made a goofy face yesterday, but it was quick and then the weight just came right back. Nothing feels genuinely funny anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I try to tell myself I should be excited about little things—like when my sister said she’d come over for coffee—but when the time comes I just feel flat. I can’t remember the last thing I actually looked forward to. Even outings with the baby feel like chores I have to survive, not enjoy.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… pretty much every day. If the baby spits up a lot, I assume it’s because my milk isn’t “good enough.” When he wouldn’t settle last night, I kept thinking it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m already failing him. I know, rationally, babies just cry… but the voice in my head keeps saying I should be handling everything better.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much all the time. I’ll be sitting on the couch, everything quiet, and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s stopped breathing in the bassinet—even though I can see his chest moving. Or I’ll worry the formula I gave him once is going to ruin his stomach forever. There’s always this tight, jittery feeling under my ribs, like something bad’s just about to happen, even when nothing’s wrong.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a few times this week. Once, I was just folding his tiny onesies and suddenly felt like I couldn’t breathe—like the walls were closing in. My hands got all shaky and I had to sit on the floor till it passed. Nothing triggered it; I just felt terrified out of nowhere. It’s happened maybe three or four nights, and each time I’m scared it means I’m losing control.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, honestly. It feels like the second I finish one feeding, the next is already due, the laundry’s piled up, the dishes are everywhere, and I can’t even think about showering. I keep telling myself, “Just get through the next hour,” but the hours stack up and I still feel like I’m drowning. I manage the basics—baby’s fed, changed, safe—but everything else feels impossible.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes… I lie down exhausted, but my head won’t stop spinning—did I burp him long enough, am I doing any of this right, will I feel like “me” again? Some nights I drift off, then jolt awake for no reason and can’t settle back. I probably get three broken hours total, and even when the baby sleeps a longer stretch, I’m still staring at the ceiling.
I have felt sad or miserable

That pretty much sums up most of my days. I wake up feeling like there’s a gray cloud hanging over me, and it just stays. I’ll cry while I’m nursing or when I’m rocking him and can’t always tell you why—just this heavy, achy sadness that won’t lift. I keep hoping tomorrow will feel lighter, but so far it hasn’t.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried almost every day this week. Sometimes it’s quiet tears while I’m changing his diaper, sometimes it turns into full-on sobbing in the bathroom because I feel like I’m failing him and I can’t explain it to anyone. It feels like the sadness just leaks out whether I want it to or not.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t thought about hurting myself. I feel low, but I’ve never wanted to end things or thought about harming myself. I just want to feel better so I can be the mom my baby needs.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 27: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – Brief Professional Note  

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia, pervasive guilt (“failing baby”), anxiety/panic attacks, insomnia, feeling overwhelmed, decreased coping.  

**Pattern**  
- Consistent dysphoric mood with anxious rumination; spontaneous panic episodes; functional impairment limited to infant care.  

**Areas of screening significance**  
- Likely meets criteria for Major Depressive Episode with Peripartum Onset; comorbid Panic/Anxiety symptoms.  

**Risk factors identified**  
- Daily crying, self-blame, sleep disruption secondary to mood, panic attacks, sense of drowning in tasks.  
- Denies self-harm ideation (no active safety concern noted).  

**Screening impression**  
- High clinical concern for moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with co-occurring anxiety; warrants expedited follow-up for formal evaluation and possible psychosocial / pharmacologic intervention.
